reading.body:
The TierPoint facility in Tulsa occupies 4,000 square feet of technical space. No IT load figure in megawatts is published on the operator's spec page, so no rack or accelerator estimate can be derived. At 4,000 square feet, the footprint is small by data center standards, and the absence of a published power figure means the campus cannot be sized against AI training or inference workloads from the information available.

The certifications tell a clear story about the intended customer base. SOC 1 Type 2 and ISO 27001 qualify the campus for enterprise and financial workloads with audit requirements. PCI DSS qualifies it for payment card data. HIPAA and HITRUST together qualify it for regulated healthcare data. ITAR qualifies it for controlled defense and export-restricted technical data. None of these certifications is specific to AI training scale, and their combination points toward compliance-driven colocation rather than large-scale compute hosting.

Within Oklahoma, this site has no published power figure, and neither do any of the other eight facilities mapped in the state. The state total of published megawatts is zero across all nine mapped facilities, so no meaningful state ranking by capacity is possible. Oklahoma as a whole, on the evidence this site holds, is not a visible participant in the published-capacity conversation that governs AI scaling decisions. This campus, like the others in the state, is not legible to that conversation until an operator publishes a power figure.
